## Bayesian Causality: Models, Accounting and the Bayesian Alternative to Double Machine Learning

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 20 results has its exact statement, its status (proved or conditional), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.0.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [Bayesian Causality: Models, Accounting and the Bayesian Alternative to Double Machine Learning](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). A textbook that builds one Bayesian model of outcomes given treatment and covariates and reads every causal quantity from its posterior, and compares it with double machine learning in simulations and in the 401(k), LaLonde and NHEFS data. Keywords: Bayesian causal inference, double machine learning, horseshoe prior, regularization induced confounding, heterogeneous treatment effects, posterior accounting identity, instrumental variables, difference in differences, sensitivity analysis and bounds, causal decisions.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23899019): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23899019 for version 1.0.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23899018 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page

- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_causality_book/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [Main result: Range of the average effect under a stable odds ratio](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html#average_effect_range_under_case_mix): Proposition 4.3, page 64, proved. With one conditional odds ratio e^psi for every unit, the average risk difference over all possible case mixes fills the interval from 0 to tanh(psi/4), so the same stable effect supports very different averages.
- [Main result: The posterior selects the group](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html#posterior_selects_the_group): Theorem 4.19, page 74, proved. The log posterior odds of one effect scale against another, or against the saturated model, move linearly in n at a rate equal to the difference of their information gaps, with a log n term for the difference in the number of parameters.
- [Main result: Exact error decomposition of the partialling out estimator](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html#exact_error_decomposition_of_the_robinson_estimator): Lemma 5.3, page 96, proved. The error of the partialling out estimator splits exactly, with no approximation, into a noise term, a cross term with mean zero under cross fitting and a bias term built from the two fitting errors, namely their product minus the effect times the squared treatment error.
- [Main result: Two channels](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html#two_channels_of_the_dml_bias): Corollary 5.4, page 98, proved. With the fits held fixed the estimator converges to the truth plus a bias fixed by the inner product of the two fitting errors and the squared treatment error.
- [Main result: No uniformly valid interval of finite length](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html#no_uniformly_valid_interval_of_finite_length): Proposition 7.8, page 149, proved. For a fixed sample size, no confidence set for the partialling out effect can both have uniform coverage over all treatment variances and have expected length bounded over that class; the proof follows Gleser and Hwang (1987) and Dufour (1997).
- [Main result: Identification of the merger effect](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html#merger_effect_depends_only_on_demand_and_conduct): Proposition 20.5, page 398, proved. Given the premerger data, the price effect of a merger is a function of the nonlinear demand parameters and the form of competition alone, so the agency question is a question about their posterior.
- [Conditional: Attenuation representation](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html#attenuation_representation): Theorem 7.5, page 142
